clue.text: Approval for the witch chant

parts.note: the Witch of Endor is the medium Saul consulted in the Bible
to chant is to sing

explanation.surface: A coven member gives her blessing to a spell sung aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: The Witch of Endor is the Old Testament medium who called up Samuel's ghost for King Saul.
explanation.definitionFit: Endorsing something is giving it your approval or backing, as when signing off a plan.

clue.text: Three points to love — a run for the grim artist

parts.note: three compass points: east, north and south
love is nil in tennis, the letter O
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A tennis score sequence somehow leads to a gloomy painter.
explanation.walkthrough: James Ensor was a Belgian painter known for macabre masks and skeletons.
explanation.definitionFit: James Ensor, the Belgian expressionist, painted grotesque, death-haunted scenes, hence grim.

clue.text: Joseph was such a visionary

explanation.surface: The biblical Joseph is praised as a man of vision.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis Joseph's brothers mock him as 'this dreamer' for his prophetic dreams.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph interpreted and had prophetic dreams; a visionary is someone given to idealistic imaginings.

clue.text: Respectable and pure perhaps when on board

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word pure in a possible alternative order

parts.note: a board can mean a table, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A decent, wholesome person serving on a committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' shuffles PURE into REPU, which sits on TABLE; 'when on' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Reputable means held in good repute, a close synonym of respectable.

clue.text: Nice set-up? US doctor holds it to be deadly

indicators.note: holds says the doctor's letters wrap around the other piece

parts.note: an interne is an American spelling of intern, a junior hospital doctor

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means the word Nice is written upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: A nice arrangement in which an American doctor finds it fatal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-up' turns NICE into ECIN, which 'holds' places inside INTERNE between its N and final E; 'it' refers back to that turned word.
explanation.definitionFit: Internecine strife is mutually destructive, so the word carries the sense of deadly or murderous.

clue.text: Starts to go at speed — stepping on it

indicators.note: the starts of the next three words give their opening letters

explanation.surface: A driver gets moving at speed, foot down hard.
explanation.walkthrough: To step on the gas is to accelerate, so 'it' in the definition stands for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas is US slang for petrol, and stepping on the accelerator pedal is stepping on the gas.

clue.text: Understood to be a historian, but not of America

indicators.note: but not of America tells us to remove the letters standing for the United States

parts.note: Tacitus was a Roman historian

explanation.surface: A chronicler of the ancient world is acknowledged, though not one from the States.
explanation.walkthrough: Tacitus wrote histories of imperial Rome; dropping US, the usual short form for America, leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit agreement is understood or implied without being spoken aloud.

clue.text: Hot unit in the corps

parts.note: RM stands for the Royal Marines, a military corps

explanation.surface: A heat-related squad within the army's ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: RM stands for the Royal Marines; 'in' just links definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A therm is a unit of heat, used in Britain for billing gas supply.

clue.text: Give international honours to girl star

parts.note: a player capped is chosen for a national side
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman is picked for the national team and becomes a sports star.
explanation.walkthrough: To cap a player is to pick them for their country, a British sporting usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Capella is the brightest star in the constellation Auriga.

clue.text: It's up to a redhead to cause fatigue

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word It is written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the 's is read as is, leaving the word it
red means the colour red
a ness is a headland, a head of land

explanation.surface: A ginger-haired person is blamed for wearing everyone out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's up' reads as 'it is up', turning IT into TI; 'redhead' splits into RED and head, which is NESS, a coastal headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiredness and fatigue are both states of weariness after exertion.

clue.text: Chief wimps back a crock

indicators.note: back tells us to read the combined chief and wimps words from the end

parts.note: top means chief or leading
wets is British slang for feeble people

explanation.surface: A boss with weaklings supporting him is a broken-down wreck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TOPWETS end to end; a wet is British slang for a feeble person.
explanation.definitionFit: A crock is an earthenware pot, so a cooking pot for stews fits.

clue.text: A cleaner defender

explanation.surface: A tidier footballer at the back of the team.
explanation.walkthrough: In football a sweeper is a defender who plays behind the main back line.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweeper is someone who sweeps floors, and also a football defender roaming behind the back line.

clue.text: Send back watch

indicators.note: back says the word for watch is read from right to left

parts.note: a timer is a watch or clock

explanation.surface: Return a timepiece.
explanation.definitionFit: To remit is to send, as with money or a case passed to another authority.

clue.text: Favoured engineers, half of them having lost blood

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, made plural as REs

indicators.note: half of takes the second two letters of the four-letter word them

parts.note: bled means lost blood

explanation.surface: Preferred engineers, half of whom have been wounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Favoured' is in the sense of a child who favours a parent, taking after them; RES treats RE (Royal Engineers) as a plural.
explanation.definitionFit: To favour a relative is to look like them, so favoured means took after in looks.

clue.text: Liable to bless cup tie maybe

indicators.note: maybe hints the letters of bless cup tie could form something else

explanation.surface: A match day blessing might be required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges all eleven letters of BLESS CUP TIE; a cup tie is a knockout football match.
explanation.definitionFit: Susceptible means prone or open to something, as liable does in liable to colds.

clue.text: Despicable man going to extremes in Corfu? Right

indicators.note: going to extremes means taking only the outermost letters of Corfu

explanation.surface: A scoundrel goes overboard on a Greek island holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to extremes' takes C and U, the first and last letters of Corfu.
explanation.definitionFit: A cur is a mongrel dog, and figuratively a contemptible, low fellow.

clue.text: Criticize players opening without one

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the other pieces stand around the numeral

parts.note: a cast is the players in a production
a gate is an opening in a wall or fence
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Attack actors who start their run lacking a lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here: CAST and GATE surround I between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To castigate is to rebuke or reprimand severely.

clue.text: Urim and Thummim were in this armour of Aaron

definitions.text: Urim and Thummim were in this armour of Aaron

parts.words: Urim and Thummim were in this armour of Aaron
parts.note: in Exodus the high priest Aaron wears a jewelled chest piece holding the sacred lots Urim and Thummim

explanation.surface: A biblical reference to the high priest's sacred vestment.
explanation.walkthrough: Exodus 28 describes the high priest's breastplate of judgement, in which the Urim and Thummim were placed.
explanation.definitionFit: A breastplate is chest armour, and Aaron's was the jewelled priestly vestment.

clue.text: Mixture for drug and French king and emperor

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis
pour is French for for, as signalled by French
R stands for rex, Latin for king
I stands for imperator, Latin for emperor

explanation.surface: A blend made up for a drug, a French monarch and an emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' turns 'for' into POUR; R and I are Rex and Imperator, as in the R.I. on old coins.
explanation.definitionFit: A potpourri is a medley, originally of dried petals, and so any assorted collection.

clue.text: Veldt, if seen in the wild, is plain

indicators.note: in the wild suggests the letters roaming loose into a new order

explanation.surface: A grassland, viewed untamed, is clearly a plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the wild' rearranges VELDT IF SEEN; 'plain' tempts as a flat grassland like the veldt, but means obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-evident means obvious without proof, and plain also means obvious or clear.

clue.text: Priest embraces friend in the island

indicators.note: embraces says the priest's letters wrap round the friend

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest
pal means friend

explanation.surface: A clergyman hugs a companion on a holiday isle.
explanation.definitionFit: La Palma is one of the Canary Islands, in the Atlantic off Africa.

clue.text: Trigonometrical ratio of the island

explanation.surface: A maths term associated with a Greek isle.
explanation.walkthrough: Cos (also Kos) is a Greek island in the Dodecanese; cos is short for cosine.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosine, abbreviated as such, is a trigonometric ratio, and the Greek isle Kos is also spelt this way.

clue.text: Girl so absorbed in a region of France

indicators.note: absorbed in says the second word goes inside the girl's name

parts.note: Cora is a girl's name
sic is Latin for so or thus

explanation.surface: A young woman is engrossed in a French district.
explanation.walkthrough: SIC is Latin for 'thus' or 'so', printed in quotations to flag an error as original.
explanation.definitionFit: Corsica is a Mediterranean island administered as a region of France.

clue.text: Carry out some simple mental process

indicators.note: some means only part of the letters of simple mental are taken

explanation.surface: Doing something basic in your head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks the run inside 'simple mental'; 'process' completes the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: To implement a plan is to carry it out or put it into effect.

clue.text: "Fairest of her daughters' not disheartened by this happening

parts.note: Milton calls Eve the fairest of her daughters in Paradise Lost

indicators.note: disheartened means the heart, the middle letter, of not is removed

explanation.surface: A line of verse about a beautiful woman being undiscouraged by an incident.
explanation.walkthrough: Paradise Lost has 'the fairest of her daughters Eve'; 'disheartened' drops O, the middle of NOT, leaving NT.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an occurrence or incident, something that happens.

clue.text: Kind of dance executed in the plant

indicators.note: executed means beheaded, so the first letter goes

parts.note: morris is a traditional English folk dance

explanation.surface: A folk dance is performed among the greenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executed' looks like 'performed' but means beheaded; a morris is an English folk dance with bells and sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: Orris is a kind of iris whose root is dried for perfume.

clue.text: A sense of location, say

indicators.note: say signals a word spoken that matches another in sound

parts.note: a site is a location

explanation.surface: Having a feel for where things are.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight is one of the five senses, vision.

clue.text: It afflicts a number of people in the island

indicators.note: in says the numeral and people go inside the island word

parts.note: an ait is a small island in a river
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
men means people

explanation.surface: A disease strikes several islanders.
explanation.walkthrough: An AIT (or eyot) is a small river island, common in Thames names.
explanation.definitionFit: An ailment is an illness, something that troubles or plagues a person.

clue.text: Principal spinner

explanation.surface: The head of a school who bowls slow.
explanation.walkthrough: A spinner is a toy top as well as a slow bowler in cricket, the false lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Top means chief or leading, and a top is a toy that spins on its point.

clue.text: Sound of 14ac in London borough

explanation.surface: The noise of a stray dog heard in the capital's suburbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 14ac is a dog, whose noise is a bark; Barking is a borough in east London.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog's noise is a bark, so its yapping fits; Barking is also an east London district.

clue.text: Specific demand

explanation.surface: A precise requirement.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact means precise, and to exact payment is to demand it.

clue.text: Preacher confused pride with hypocrisy

indicators.note: confused suggests the letters of pride jumbled

parts.note: cant is insincere, hypocritical talk

explanation.surface: A preacher muddled vanity with insincerity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' scrambles PRIDE into PREDI, and CANT follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A predicant is a preaching friar or minister, especially a Dominican.
